title: pkix-dane: confirm the no_std dependency tree on a bare-metal target
description:
## What

pkix-dane claims no_std. Source-level no_std IS verified: building with default features puts #![no_std] in force, and a probe referencing std:: fails to compile while the same probe compiles under --features std.

NOT verified: that the dependency tree resolves and builds for an actual bare-metal target. The environment where pkix-dane was written could not install one — rustup lives in /usr/local/rustup and 'rustup target add thumbv7em-none-eabi' fails with 'error opening file for download: cleaning up cached downloads: No such file or directory (os error 2)'.

## Why it is expected to pass

pkix-dane's non-optional dependencies are pkix-path, x509-cert, der and sha2, all pinned default-features = false at the workspace level. Per commit 5a3ed995, pkix-path already builds for riscv64gc-unknown-none-elf and thumbv7em-none-eabi on exactly that stack. So this is confirmation, not expected discovery.

## Note from that commit worth carrying

x86_64-unknown-none needs RUSTFLAGS='--cfg sha2_backend="soft"' because of an LLVM error in sha2 0.11's SHA-NI backend on that soft-float target. pkix-dane depends on sha2 directly (matching types 1 and 2 are SHA-256 and SHA-512), so it inherits that constraint. Worth checking whether pkix-dane's docs should mention it — pkix-path's apparently do not.

## How

    rustup target add thumbv7em-none-eabi riscv64gc-unknown-none-elf
    cargo build -p pkix-dane --target thumbv7em-none-eabi
    cargo build -p pkix-dane --target riscv64gc-unknown-none-elf
    # and, with the soft backend:
    RUSTFLAGS='--cfg sha2_backend="soft"' cargo build -p pkix-dane --target x86_64-unknown-none

A minute's work for anyone with a writable rustup.

## Acceptance

[ ] pkix-dane builds for thumbv7em-none-eabi and riscv64gc-unknown-none-elf
[ ] Any target-specific RUSTFLAGS requirement is documented in the crate or its README
close_reason:
FIXED 2026-11-24. Verified, and gated so it cannot regress silently.

## The blocker named in this bead is gone

It recorded that rustup could not install a bare-metal target here: /usr/local/rustup is not writable and the attempt failed. That was true at the time. It stopped being true when the MSRV work (PKIX-z2g4) needed a 1.88 toolchain and installed one into a writable RUSTUP_HOME under the session scratchpad — the targets went into the same place without trouble.

Worth noting as a pattern: a bead blocked on "the environment cannot do X" is worth retrying after unrelated work has changed the environment, rather than staying blocked on a snapshot of it.

## Result, wider than the bead asked

All EIGHT crates carrying the no-std category build for all three targets:

                     thumbv7em  riscv64gc  x86_64-none
  pkix-ac                ok         ok          ok
  pkix-aia               ok         ok          ok
  pkix-composite         ok         ok          ok
  pkix-dane              ok         ok          ok
  pkix-dnssec-anchor     ok         ok          ok
  pkix-identity          ok         ok          ok
  pkix-path              ok         ok          ok
  pkix-path-builder      ok         ok          ok

(x86_64-unknown-none with the soft SHA-2 backend; see below.)

## The sha2 constraint: confirmed, not inherited on faith

This bead carried forward a note from commit 5a3ed995 that x86_64-unknown-none needs RUSTFLAGS='--cfg sha2_backend="soft"'. That was worth checking rather than repeating, and it holds:

- without the flag: rustc-LLVM ERROR: Do not know how to split the result of this operator! while compiling sha2 0.11
- with the flag: clean

So it is necessary and sufficient, and it is sha2's constraint rather than this workspace's — pkix-path inherits it too. It surfaces in pkix-dane because matching types 1 and 2 are SHA-256 and SHA-512, so that crate depends on sha2 directly.

Documented in pkix-dane's crate-level rustdoc, where a consumer meets it, and applied as its OWN CI step rather than folded into the main loop — so if a future sha2 release fixes the LLVM problem, that step starts passing without the flag and says so, instead of the flag being carried indefinitely.

## Gated, which is the durable part

A one-off verification would have gone stale the next time a dependency changed, which is precisely the failure this workspace just fixed for the MSRV. The new no-std job in quality-gates.yml derives its crate list from the no-std CATEGORY in each manifest rather than hardcoding it, so:

- adding the category to a crate opts it into the gate
- a crate that cannot hold the claim fails in CI rather than in a consumer's firmware build

It builds libraries only. A bare-metal binary needs a global allocator, which is the consumer's to supply, so cargo build -p on the library is the right scope.

## Two findings outside scope

- pkix-lint and pkix-profiles do NOT build for bare metal, and correctly do not claim the no-std category: neither declares #![no_std], and pkix-lint uses std::borrow::Cow directly. So the metadata was already accurate and this test confirmed it rather than catching anything. Pleasant result: the no-std category turns out to be a reliable predictor across the workspace.
- pkix-revocation DOES build for all three bare-metal targets but does not carry the category, so its metadata understates what it supports. Left alone deliberately: adding the category opts it into the new gate, which is a commitment worth making on purpose rather than as a side effect of a verification pass. Worth a small bead if anyone wants it claimed.

## Acceptance

[x] pkix-dane builds for thumbv7em-none-eabi and riscv64gc-unknown-none-elf — and for x86_64-unknown-none with the documented flag, and so do the other seven no-std crates
[x] Any target-specific RUSTFLAGS requirement documented — in pkix-dane's crate docs and in the CI job's comments, with the reason it is a separate step

## Residual

The CI job has not run on GitHub; it is verified locally against a real 1.88 toolchain with the three targets installed. Same caveat as the other workflows added today.
